title: ID0464585/DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2/R3312881977039] Charger does not show Outlets
description:

Solution: Manual re-build of CFast card with provided config files, charger now working fine. Ticket can be closed

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0464585/DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2/R3312881977039] Charger does not show Outlets CRM:02681001152
additional_info.body:
Hi Younes,
The charger is unable to connect to SCB, we have already tried this.
This is an out of box failure that we picked up prior to shipping to our customer.  The config is incomplete (hawkbit.conf missing from the data partition) and there is something very wrong with the configuration that means the sicharge-cp-backend is not communicating with the front end of the charger.
We have tried configuring the routers separately in order to see if logs are pushed to SCB but no connection is made.
We have also tried using companion tool, but the MQTT browser is unable to connect to the PLC.
There does not seem to be a hardware problem, as noted in the initial ticket we tried a different CFast card from another charger (so configured as another serial), the charger booted up fine, connected to SCB and was able to be connected to via companion tool.  This of course was only temporary as we cannot have this charger masquerading as another serial number.
We can re-build the CFast card, but need the Config File package for this charger.
Many Regards,
Aaron Gillon

Good morning Aaron,
I am reaching out as SichargeD Expert in regards of ticket
ID0464585.
Thank you for your detailed report and explanation why you need the config files. You can find them attached to this email.
I understand your reason why you want to flash a CFast card, but I would like to suggest also a different point of view: I am aware you were in contact with Ferdinand and Benjamin from our R&D department in regards of connectivity with AWS servers in NZ when chargers were running on FW v7.0.5.
In case this AWS server issue is not solved yet (I know a solution has been found, what is missing is an implementation for the whole NZ fleet), just to avoid any influence of syncing of charger configurations from the servers, I may suggest to flash the CFast card with the new config files and with a FW v6.X.
Just food for thoughts.
Please let me know if you require further support for this ticket or we can close it.

Hi Aaron, good afternoon. I hope you are doing well.
Since Fosco is on vacation, I will take over.
I can tell you that
no charger leaves the factory without being tested 100%
, and there are internal documents to prove it.
To be able to ascertain where the fault lies, we need to collect a certain number of traces with Live Linux. If this ever happens again, please run the Live Linux script called "Dump-data". This will collect all the logs of the system and R&D can make an investigation.
For now, since the problem is solved I will close the ticket.
Thank you very much and have a lovely holiday season.
Best regards,
Francisco
